operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 11876 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The sole paragraph creates a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), directs it to report within 30 days from the date of the order, and restates the section 10 status-quo period from the date of the order until 30 days after the report. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end; when it ran out depends on the unrecorded report date. No earlier express end was found.

Title 3— The President
Executive Order 11876 •  September 2, 1975
Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between the
Carriers Represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and
Certain of Their Employees
\  .; %
A  dispute exists between the carriers represented by the National 
Railway Labor Conference, designated in lists attached hereto and made 
a part hereof, and certain of their employees represented by the Railway 
Employes’ Department, AFL— C IO ; International Brotherhood of Boiler­
makers, Iron Ship Builders, Blacksmiths, Forgers & Helpers; Brotherhood 
Railway Carmen of United States and Canada; International Brother­
hood of Electrical Workers and the International Brotherhood of Fire­
men & Oilers;
This dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
This dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such 
as to deprive a section of the country of essential transportation service:
N O W , TH E R EFO R E, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute. N o member of the board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any 
carrier.
The Board shall report its finding to the President with respect to the 
dispute within 30 days from the date of this Order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for 30 days after the board Has made its report to 
the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 11969, whose subject line describes the administration of the Emergency Natural Gas Act of 1977. Section 1 delegates to the Chairman of the Federal Power Commission all of the President’s authority under the Emergency Natural Gas Act of 1977 except the authority to declare and terminate a natural gas emergency under section 3 of that Act. Executive Order 12038 (signed 1978-02-03, effective as of 1977-10-01 under its section 6) amended section 1 by deleting its second sentence and by substituting the Secretary of Energy for the Chairman of the Federal Power Commission; before: the authority was delegated to the Chairman and the second sentence said the delegation was not to the Commission as a collective body; after: the authority is delegated to the Secretary of Energy and that sentence is gone. The clause continues, amended, under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (strike-and-insert); the substance of the delegatee changed. No earlier express end was found.

Executive Order 12038 •. February 3,1978
Relating to Certain Functions Transferred to the Secretary of Energy by the 
Department of Energy Organization Act
By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United States  
of America, in order to reflect the responsibilities of the Secretary of Energy  
for the performance of certain functions previously vested in other officers of  
the United States by direction of the President and subsequently transferred to  
the Secretary of Energy pursuant to the Department of Energy Organization  
Act (91 Stat. 565; 42 U.S.C. 7101 et seq.), it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. Functions o f the Federal Energy Administration. In accordance with  
the transfer of all functions vested by law in the Federal Energy Administra­
tion, or the Administrator thereof, to the Secretary of Energy pursuant to  
Section 301(a) of the Department of Energy Organization Act, hereinafter  
referred to as the Act, the Executive Orders and Proclamations referred to in  
this Section, which conferred authority or responsibility upon the Administra­
tor of the Federal Energy Administration, are amended as follows:
(a) Executive Order No. 11647, as amended, relating to Federal Regional  
Councils, is further amended by deleting “The Federal Energy Administra­
tion” in Section l(a)(10) and substituting “The Department of Energy”, and  
by deleting “The Deputy Administrator of the Federal Energy Administration”  
in Section 3(a)(10) and substituting “The Deputy Secretary of Energy”.
(b) Executive Order No. 11790 of June 25, 1974, relating to the Federal  
Energy Administration Act of 1974, is amended by deleting “Administrator of  
the Federal Energy Administration” and “Administrator” wherever they  
appear in Sections 1  through 6 and substituting “Secretary of Energy” and  
“Secretary”, respectively, and by deleting Section 7 through 10.
(c) Executive Order No. 11912, as amended, relating to energy policy and  
conservation, and Proclamation No. 3279, as amended, relating to imports of  
petroleum and petroleum products, are further amended by deleting ^Admin­
istrator of the Federal Energy Administration”, “Federal Energy Administra­
tion”, and “Administrator” (when used in reference to the Federal Energy 
Administration) wherever those terms appear and by substituting “Secretary of  
Energy”, “Department of Energy”, and “Secretary”, respectively, and by de­
leting “and the Administrator of Energy Research and Development” in Sec­
tion 1(b) of Executive Order No. 11912, as .amended.
S e c. 2. Functions o f the Federal Power Commission. In accordance with the  
transfer of functions vested in the Federal Power Commission to the Secretary  
of Energy pursuant to Section 301(b) of the Act, the Executive Orders re­
ferred to in this Section, which conferred authority or responsibility upon the  
Federal Power Commission, or Chairman thereof, are amended or modified as  
follows:
(a) Executive Order No. 10485 of September 3, 1953, relating to certain  
facilities at the borders of the United States is amended by deleting Section 2  
thereof, and by deleting “Federal Power Commission” and “Commission”

Section 1. There is hereby delegated to the Chairman of the Federal Power 
Commission, hereafter the Chairman, all of the authority vested in the President 
by the Emergency Natural Gas Act of 1977, except for the authority to declare and 
terminate a natural gas emergency pursuant to Section 3 of said Act. Nothing in such 
delegation shall be construed as delegating such authority to the Federal Power Com­
mission as a collective body, except insofar as the Chairman may further delegate his 
authority under Section 3 of this Order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 11969, whose subject line describes the administration of the Emergency Natural Gas Act of 1977. Section 2 directs the Chairman to consult, to the extent he deems appropriate, with the Secretary of the Interior, the Administrator of the Federal Energy Administration, other Commission members and the heads of other Executive agencies. Executive Order 12038 amended section 2 by deleting the other consulted officers and substituting the Secretary of Energy for the Chairman; before: the Chairman consulted the Secretary of the Interior, the Federal Energy Administration Administrator, other Commission members and other agency heads; after: the Secretary consults the heads of other Executive agencies. The clause continues, amended. No earlier express end was found.

leting “and the Administrator of Energy Research and Development” in Sec­

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 11969, whose subject line describes the administration of the Emergency Natural Gas Act of 1977. Section 3 permits the Chairman to delegate the authority further, in whole or in part, to any other officer or Executive agency. Executive Order 12038 substituted the Secretary of Energy for the Chairman in section 3; before: the Chairman may further delegate; after: the Secretary may further delegate. The clause continues, amended. No earlier express end was found.

Title 3—The President
Executive Order 12038 •. February 3,1978
Relating to Certain Functions Transferred to the Secretary of Energy by the 
Department of Energy Organization Act
By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United States  
of America, in order to reflect the responsibilities of the Secretary of Energy  
for the performance of certain functions previously vested in other officers of  
the United States by direction of the President and subsequently transferred to  
the Secretary of Energy pursuant to the Department of Energy Organization  
Act (91 Stat. 565; 42 U.S.C. 7101 et seq.), it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. Functions o f the Federal Energy Administration. In accordance with  
the transfer of all functions vested by law in the Federal Energy Administra­
tion, or the Administrator thereof, to the Secretary of Energy pursuant to  
Section 301(a) of the Department of Energy Organization Act, hereinafter  
referred to as the Act, the Executive Orders and Proclamations referred to in  
this Section, which conferred authority or responsibility upon the Administra­
tor of the Federal Energy Administration, are amended as follows:
(a) Executive Order No. 11647, as amended, relating to Federal Regional  
Councils, is further amended by deleting “The Federal Energy Administra­
tion” in Section l(a)(10) and substituting “The Department of Energy”, and  
by deleting “The Deputy Administrator of the Federal Energy Administration”  
in Section 3(a)(10) and substituting “The Deputy Secretary of Energy”.
(b) Executive Order No. 11790 of June 25, 1974, relating to the Federal  
Energy Administration Act of 1974, is amended by deleting “Administrator of  
the Federal Energy Administration” and “Administrator” wherever they  
appear in Sections 1  through 6 and substituting “Secretary of Energy” and  
“Secretary”, respectively, and by deleting Section 7 through 10.
(c) Executive Order No. 11912, as amended, relating to energy policy and  
conservation, and Proclamation No. 3279, as amended, relating to imports of  
petroleum and petroleum products, are further amended by deleting ^Admin­
istrator of the Federal Energy Administration”, “Federal Energy Administra­
tion”, and “Administrator” (when used in reference to the Federal Energy 
Administration) wherever those terms appear and by substituting “Secretary of  
Energy”, “Department of Energy”, and “Secretary”, respectively, and by de­
leting “and the Administrator of Energy Research and Development” in Sec­
tion 1(b) of Executive Order No. 11912, as .amended.
S e c. 2. Functions o f the Federal Power Commission. In accordance with the  
transfer of functions vested in the Federal Power Commission to the Secretary  
of Energy pursuant to Section 301(b) of the Act, the Executive Orders re­
ferred to in this Section, which conferred authority or responsibility upon the  
Federal Power Commission, or Chairman thereof, are amended or modified as  
follows:
(a) Executive Order No. 10485 of September 3, 1953, relating to certain  
facilities at the borders of the United States is amended by deleting Section 2  
thereof, and by deleting “Federal Power Commission” and “Commission”

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 11969, whose subject line describes the administration of the Emergency Natural Gas Act of 1977. Section 4 directs the heads of Executive agencies to cooperate with and assist the Chairman. Executive Order 12038 substituted the Secretary of Energy for the Chairman in section 4; before: agency heads assist the Chairman; after: they assist the Secretary. The clause continues, amended. No earlier express end was found.

Title 3—The President
Executive Order 12038 •. February 3,1978
Relating to Certain Functions Transferred to the Secretary of Energy by the 
Department of Energy Organization Act
By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United States  
of America, in order to reflect the responsibilities of the Secretary of Energy  
for the performance of certain functions previously vested in other officers of  
the United States by direction of the President and subsequently transferred to  
the Secretary of Energy pursuant to the Department of Energy Organization  
Act (91 Stat. 565; 42 U.S.C. 7101 et seq.), it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. Functions o f the Federal Energy Administration. In accordance with  
the transfer of all functions vested by law in the Federal Energy Administra­
tion, or the Administrator thereof, to the Secretary of Energy pursuant to  
Section 301(a) of the Department of Energy Organization Act, hereinafter  
referred to as the Act, the Executive Orders and Proclamations referred to in  
this Section, which conferred authority or responsibility upon the Administra­
tor of the Federal Energy Administration, are amended as follows:
(a) Executive Order No. 11647, as amended, relating to Federal Regional  
Councils, is further amended by deleting “The Federal Energy Administra­
tion” in Section l(a)(10) and substituting “The Department of Energy”, and  
by deleting “The Deputy Administrator of the Federal Energy Administration”  
in Section 3(a)(10) and substituting “The Deputy Secretary of Energy”.
(b) Executive Order No. 11790 of June 25, 1974, relating to the Federal  
Energy Administration Act of 1974, is amended by deleting “Administrator of  
the Federal Energy Administration” and “Administrator” wherever they  
appear in Sections 1  through 6 and substituting “Secretary of Energy” and  
“Secretary”, respectively, and by deleting Section 7 through 10.
(c) Executive Order No. 11912, as amended, relating to energy policy and  
conservation, and Proclamation No. 3279, as amended, relating to imports of  
petroleum and petroleum products, are further amended by deleting ^Admin­
istrator of the Federal Energy Administration”, “Federal Energy Administra­
tion”, and “Administrator” (when used in reference to the Federal Energy 
Administration) wherever those terms appear and by substituting “Secretary of  
Energy”, “Department of Energy”, and “Secretary”, respectively, and by de­
leting “and the Administrator of Energy Research and Development” in Sec­
tion 1(b) of Executive Order No. 11912, as .amended.
S e c. 2. Functions o f the Federal Power Commission. In accordance with the  
transfer of functions vested in the Federal Power Commission to the Secretary  
of Energy pursuant to Section 301(b) of the Act, the Executive Orders re­
ferred to in this Section, which conferred authority or responsibility upon the  
Federal Power Commission, or Chairman thereof, are amended or modified as  
follows:
(a) Executive Order No. 10485 of September 3, 1953, relating to certain  
facilities at the borders of the United States is amended by deleting Section 2  
thereof, and by deleting “Federal Power Commission” and “Commission”

amended by substituting “Secretary of Energy” for “Secretary of the Interior”,  
by adding “of the Interior” after “Secretary” in Sections 2 and 3, and by  
adding “and the Secretary of Energy,” after “the Secretary of the Interior”  
wherever the latter term appears in Section 5.

Columbia River Treaty, is amended by deleting “Secretary of the Interior”

ing therefor “Secretary of Energy” and “Department of Energy”, respectively.

provide that all such functions shall be exercised by (1) the Secretary of

the extent consistent with the functions of the Atomic Energy Commission  
that were transferred to the Commission by the Energy Reorganization Act of

(2) Executive Order No. 11652, as amended, relating to the classification  
of national security matters, is further amended by substituting “Department

Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 11969, whose subject line describes the administration of the Emergency Natural Gas Act of 1977. Section 5 directs Executive agencies to provide the Chairman, to the extent permitted by law, administrative support and information on request. Executive Order 12038 substituted the Secretary of Energy for the Chairman in section 5; before: agencies support the Chairman; after: they support the Secretary. The clause continues, amended. No earlier express end was found.

Title 3—The President
Executive Order 12038 •. February 3,1978
Relating to Certain Functions Transferred to the Secretary of Energy by the 
Department of Energy Organization Act
By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United States  
of America, in order to reflect the responsibilities of the Secretary of Energy  
for the performance of certain functions previously vested in other officers of  
the United States by direction of the President and subsequently transferred to  
the Secretary of Energy pursuant to the Department of Energy Organization  
Act (91 Stat. 565; 42 U.S.C. 7101 et seq.), it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. Functions o f the Federal Energy Administration. In accordance with  
the transfer of all functions vested by law in the Federal Energy Administra­
tion, or the Administrator thereof, to the Secretary of Energy pursuant to  
Section 301(a) of the Department of Energy Organization Act, hereinafter  
referred to as the Act, the Executive Orders and Proclamations referred to in  
this Section, which conferred authority or responsibility upon the Administra­
tor of the Federal Energy Administration, are amended as follows:
(a) Executive Order No. 11647, as amended, relating to Federal Regional  
Councils, is further amended by deleting “The Federal Energy Administra­
tion” in Section l(a)(10) and substituting “The Department of Energy”, and  
by deleting “The Deputy Administrator of the Federal Energy Administration”  
in Section 3(a)(10) and substituting “The Deputy Secretary of Energy”.
(b) Executive Order No. 11790 of June 25, 1974, relating to the Federal  
Energy Administration Act of 1974, is amended by deleting “Administrator of  
the Federal Energy Administration” and “Administrator” wherever they  
appear in Sections 1  through 6 and substituting “Secretary of Energy” and  
“Secretary”, respectively, and by deleting Section 7 through 10.
(c) Executive Order No. 11912, as amended, relating to energy policy and  
conservation, and Proclamation No. 3279, as amended, relating to imports of  
petroleum and petroleum products, are further amended by deleting ^Admin­
istrator of the Federal Energy Administration”, “Federal Energy Administra­
tion”, and “Administrator” (when used in reference to the Federal Energy 
Administration) wherever those terms appear and by substituting “Secretary of  
Energy”, “Department of Energy”, and “Secretary”, respectively, and by de­
leting “and the Administrator of Energy Research and Development” in Sec­
tion 1(b) of Executive Order No. 11912, as .amended.
S e c. 2. Functions o f the Federal Power Commission. In accordance with the  
transfer of functions vested in the Federal Power Commission to the Secretary  
of Energy pursuant to Section 301(b) of the Act, the Executive Orders re­
ferred to in this Section, which conferred authority or responsibility upon the  
Federal Power Commission, or Chairman thereof, are amended or modified as  
follows:
(a) Executive Order No. 10485 of September 3, 1953, relating to certain  
facilities at the borders of the United States is amended by deleting Section 2  
thereof, and by deleting “Federal Power Commission” and “Commission”

THE PRESIDENT 6791
Executive O rder 11969 • February 2 , 1977
Administration of the Emergency Natural Gas Act of 1977
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and statutes of the 
United States of America, including .Section 13 of the Emergency Natural Gas Act 
of 1977 (Public Law 95-2), and Section 301 of Title 3 of the United States Code, 
and as President.of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. There is hereby delegated to the Chairman of the Federal Power 
Commission, hereafter the Chairman, all of the authority vested in the President 
by the Emergency Natural Gas Act of 1977, except for the authority to declare and 
terminate a natural gas emergency pursuant to Section 3 of said Act. Nothing in such 
delegation shall be construed as delegating such authority to the Federal Power Com­
mission as a collective body, except insofar as the Chairman may further delegate his 
authority under Section 3 of this Order.
Sec. 2. The Chairman shall, to the extent he deems appropriate, consult with 
the Secretary of the Interior, the Administrator of the Federal Energy Administration, 
other members of the Federal Power.Commission and the heads of other Executive 
agencies in exercising the authority delegated to him by this Order.
Sec. 3. All authority delegated to the Chairman by this Order may be further dele­
gated, in whole or in part, by the Chairman to any other officer of the United 
States or to any Executive agency.
Sec. 4. The heads of all Executive agencies shall cooperate with and assist the 
Chairman in carrying out the authority delegated to him by this Order.
Sec. 5. All Executive agencies shall, to the extent permitted by law, provide the 
Chairman on request such administrative support and information as may be neces­
sary to carry out the authority delegated to him by this Order.
T he W hite  H ouse ,
February 2, 1977.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11969 (42 FR 6791, Federal Register of February 4, 1977; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Administration of the Emergency Natural Gas Act of 1977 and signed February 2, 1977. It delegates the President’s authority under the Emergency Natural Gas Act of 1977 to the Chairman of the Federal Power Commission. Inventory: five numbered sections, confirmed against the full held text, each recorded as one clause. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 11969, whose subject line describes the administration of the Emergency Natural Gas Act of 1977. Executive Order 12038 of February 3, 1978, effective as of October 1, 1977 under its own section 6, amended sections 1 to 5 as recorded in each clause; it is an amendment and a later event, not an end. The statute text (Public Law 95-2) is not held; any expiry of that Act is an unnamed instrument and a disclosed candidate only (owner ruling 2026-10-21, unnamed instruments).  The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found citations of this number outside its own printings only in the printings of EO 12038. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12097, whose subject line describes standards and guidelines for the merit selection of United States district judges. Section 1-101 directs that, whenever a district court vacancy occurs, the President shall nominate a person whose character, experience, ability and commitment to equal justice qualify that person to serve. No earlier express end was found.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
1-101. Whenever a vacancy occurs in a district court of the United States,  
the President shall nominate as district judge to fill that vacancy a person  
whose character, experience, ability, and commitment to equal justice under  
law qualifies that person to serve in the federal judiciary.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12097, whose subject line describes standards and guidelines for the merit selection of United States district judges. Section 1-102 directs the Attorney General to assist the President by recommending and evaluating persons for district judgeships and to receive recommendations from any person, commission or organization. No earlier express end was found.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
1-102. The Attorney General shall assist the President by recommending  
to the President persons to be considered for appointment who are qualified  
to be district judges and by evaluating potential nominees. The Attorney  
General shall receive recommendations of such persons from any person,  
commission or organization.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12097, whose subject line describes standards and guidelines for the merit selection of United States district judges. Section 1-103 encourages the use of commissions to notify the public of vacancies and recommend district judges and directs the Attorney General to make public suggested guidelines for such commissions. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12097, whose subject line describes standards and guidelines for the merit selection of United States district judges. Section 1-104 directs the Attorney General, before making recommendations, to consider whether public notice and an affirmative effort to identify qualified candidates were made, whether the selection process was fair and reasonable, and whether the persons recommended meet the standards of section 1-2. No earlier express end was found.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
1-104. Before making recommendations, the Attorney General shall con­
sider whether:
(a) Public notice of the vacancy has been given and an affirmative effort  
has been made, in the case of each vacancy, to identify qualified candidates,  
including women and members of minority groups;
(b) The selection process was fair and reasonable;
(c) The person or persons recommended meet the standards for evalua­
tion set forth in Section 1-2 o f this Order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12097, whose subject line describes standards and guidelines for the merit selection of United States district judges. Section 1-105 provides that proposed nominees are evaluated with consideration of Department of Justice investigation reports and other relevant information. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12097, whose subject line describes standards and guidelines for the merit selection of United States district judges. Section 1-201 sets the standards (subsections (a) to (g)) for determining whether a person is qualified to serve as a district judge. No earlier express end was found.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
1-201. The standards to be used in determining whether a person is  
qualified to serve as a district judge are whether that person:
(a) Is a citizen of the United States, is a member of a bar of a state,  
territory, possession or the District o f Columbia, and is in good standing in  
every bar in which that person is a member;
(b) Possesses, and has a reputation for, integrity, good character, and  
common sense;
(c) Is, and has a reputation for being, fair, experienced, even-tempered  
and free of biases against any class of citizens or any religious or racial group;
(d) Is of sound physical and mental health;
(e) Possesses and has demonstrated commitment to equal justice under
law;
FEDERAL REGISTER, V O L  43, NO. 219— M ONDAY, NOVEMBER 13, 1978

=== PDF page 14 of 224 ===
52456 THE PRESIDENT
(f) Possesses and has demonstrated outstanding legal ability and compe­
tence, as evidenced by substantial legal experience, ability to deal with com­
plex legal problems, aptitude for legal scholarship and writing, and familiarity  
with courts and their processes;
(g) Has the ability and the willingness to manage complicated pretrial and  
trial proceedings,1  including the ability to weigh conflicting testimony and  
make factual determinations, and to communicate skillfully with jurors and  
witnesses.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12097, whose subject line describes standards and guidelines for the merit selection of United States district judges. Section 1-301 amends section 3(b) of Executive Order 12059 of May 11, 1978 so that the Panel for the District of Columbia Circuit also recommends nominees for the United States District Court for the District of Columbia using the standards of this order. Executive Order 12305 also revokes Executive Order 12059 as amended without naming this order; under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments) that is a disclosed candidate earlier end for the reviewer and not an end, since the revocation of the parent does not name the amendment. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation of the amended order. Executive Order 12305 of May 5, 1981 (46 FR 25421, Federal Register of May 7, 1981; held government printing) revokes Executive Order 12084 of September 27, 1978, as amended by Executive Order 12097 of November 8, 1978, and terminates the committee it created; the enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the end is dated on signing, 1981-05-05 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). This clause only amends Executive Order 12084, so it has no operation once that order is revoked. Section 1-302 amends Executive Order 12084 of September 27, 1978: paragraph (1) rewrites section 1-202(d) and paragraph (2) rewrites section 1-203 so that the Commission uses the standards of this order. Executive Order 12110 (December 28, 1978, effective December 31, 1978) continued the committee created by Executive Order 12084 until December 31, 1980; that continuance is a later event and not an end. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 later revoked this order by number; it is a later event because the clause had already ended. No earlier end was found.

Title 3— The President
Executive Order 12097 •  November 8,1978
Standards and Guidelines for the Merit Selection of United States District Judges
By virtue of the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution  
and the statutes of the United States of America, including Section.7(a) of the  
Omnibus Judgeship Act of 1978, providing that the President shall promulgate  
and publish standards and guidelines for the selection of nominees for United  
States district court judgeships, it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-1. Nomination o f  D istrict Judges.
1-101. Whenever a vacancy occurs in a district court of the United States,  
the President shall nominate as district judge to fill that vacancy a person  
whose character, experience, ability, and commitment to equal justice under  
law qualifies that person to serve in the federal judiciary.
1-102. The Attorney General shall assist the President by recommending  
to the President persons to be considered for appointment who are qualified  
to be district judges and by evaluating potential nominees. The Attorney  
General shall receive recommendations of such persons from any person,  
commission or organization.
1-103. The use o f commissions to notify the public of vacancies and to  
make recommendations for district judge is encouraged. The Attorney Gen­
eral shall make public the suggested guidelines for such commissions.
. 1-104. Before making recommendations, the Attorney General shall con­
sider whether:
(a) Public notice of the vacancy has been given and an affirmative effort  
has been made, in the case of each vacancy, to identify qualified candidates,  
including women and members of minority groups;
(b) The selection process was fair and reasonable;
(c) The person or persons recommended meet the standards for evalua­
tion set forth in Section 1-2 o f this Order.
1-105. In evaluating proposed nominees, consideration will be given to  
reports o f Department o f Justice investigations and all other relevant informa­
tion concerning potential nominees and their qualifications.
1-2. Standards f o r  E valuating Proposed Nominees.
1-201. The standards to be used in determining whether a person is  
qualified to serve as a district judge are whether that person:
(a) Is a citizen of the United States, is a member of a bar of a state,  
territory, possession or the District o f Columbia, and is in good standing in  
every bar in which that person is a member;
(b) Possesses, and has a reputation for, integrity, good character, and  
common sense;
(c) Is, and has a reputation for being, fair, experienced, even-tempered  
and free of biases against any class of citizens or any religious or racial group;
(d) Is of sound physical and mental health;
(e) Possesses and has demonstrated commitment to equal justice under
law;
FEDERAL REGISTER, V O L  43, NO. 219— M ONDAY, NOVEMBER 13, 1978

tence, as evidenced by substantial legal experience, ability to deal with com­
plex legal problems, aptitude for legal scholarship and writing, and familiarity  
with courts and their processes;
(g) Has the ability and the willingness to manage complicated pretrial and  
trial proceedings,1  including the ability to weigh conflicting testimony and

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12097 (43 FR 52455, Federal Register of November 13, 1978; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Standards and Guidelines for the Merit Selection of United States District Judges and signed November 8, 1978. The dossier’s automatic split produced twelve fragments, including a duplicated group of subsections (a) to (c), and did not record sections 1-101, 1-102, 1-103, 1-105 and 1-301 as units. The operative commands are the eight numbered sections 1-101 to 1-105, 1-201, 1-301 and 1-302 of the original; the headings 1-1, 1-2 and 1-3 and the date line are not commands. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12097, whose subject line describes standards and guidelines for the merit selection of United States district judges. Section 1-302 ended earlier, on 1981-05-05, because Executive Order 12305 revoked the order it amended, naming this order; the other seven clauses end on 1986-02-25 and the whole-order end is the later date. The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found citations of this number outside its own printings only in the printings of EO 12305. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12140, whose subject line describes delegating authorities relating to motor gasoline end-user allocation. Section 1-101 delegates to each Governor the authority to establish a system of end-user allocation for motor gasoline, subject to the terms set out in the order. The sunset sentence of section 1-105 was deleted by Executive Order 12162 before it operated, so no own-terms end applies to this clause. No earlier express end was found.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Section 1-101. Each Governor is hereby delegated the authority to establish a 
system of end-user allocation for motor gasoline, subject to the terms and  
conditions as set forth below.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12140, whose subject line describes delegating authorities relating to motor gasoline end-user allocation. Section 1-102 lets a Governor who determines that a shortage of motor gasoline endangers public health, safety or welfare require retail outlets to supply vehicles by odd or even license-plate days, to require minimum purchases, or to supply gasoline at specified times or days. The sunset sentence of section 1-105 was deleted by Executive Order 12162 before it operated, so no own-terms end applies to this clause. No earlier express end was found.

Federal Register / Vol. 44, No. 192 / Tuesday, October 2, 1979 / Presidential Documents 56665
Presidential Documents
Executive Order 12162 of September 28, 1979
Amendment to Executive Order 12140
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of 
the United States of America, including the Emergency Petroleum Allocation 
A ct of 1973, as amended (15 U .S.C . 751 et se q .), Executive Order No. 12140 is 
hereby amended by deleting the first sentence in Sec. 1-105.
THE W HITE H O U SE, 
Septem ber 28, 1979.
[FR Doc. 79-30633  
Filed 9-26-79; 4:50 pm]  
Billing code 3195-01-M

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express deletion. The first sentence of section 1-105 provided that the order terminates, unless extended, at midnight on September 30, 1979. Executive Order 12162 of September 28, 1979 (44 FR 56665, Federal Register of October 2, 1979; held government printing) amends this order by deleting that sentence; it states no effective date, so the end is dated on signing, 1979-09-28 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer), two days before the sunset would have operated. The deleted sunset therefore never ended the order. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 later revoked the order by number; it is a later event because this clause had already ended. No earlier end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12140, whose subject line describes delegating authorities relating to motor gasoline end-user allocation. The second sentence of section 1-105 lets the Secretary of Energy at any time revoke the delegation in whole or in part and with respect to any State. The sunset sentence of section 1-105 was deleted by Executive Order 12162 before it operated, so no own-terms end applies to this clause. No earlier express end was found.

The dossier’s automatic split (a lead fragment and fragments (a), (a)(1), (a)(2) and (c)) covered only part of section 1-102 and omitted sections 1-101, 1-103, 1-104 and 1-105 as units. The operative commands are the sections 1-101 to 1-104 and the two sentences of section 1-105 of the original; the page-break header and the date line are not commands. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12140, whose subject line describes delegating authorities relating to motor gasoline end-user allocation. The sunset sentence of section 1-105 was deleted by Executive Order 12162 (1979-09-28), which is the first end of that clause; the other clauses end on 1986-02-25. Whether the authority of the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973 lapsed before 1986 is not established from held sources (the statute text is not held), and such a lapse would be an unnamed instrument and a disclosed candidate only. Executive Order 12287 of January 28, 1981 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12287.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) exempted all crude oil and refined petroleum products from the price and allocation controls adopted under that Act without naming this order; it is likewise a disclosed candidate earlier end and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12153, whose subject line describes decontrolling heavy oil. Section 1-101 exempts, effective August 17, 1979, prices charged in the first sale of heavy crude oil from price controls adopted under the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973 and defines heavy crude oil as crude oil of 16.0 degrees API gravity or less. Executive Order 12186 (1979-12-21) replaced the 16.0 figure with 20.0 degrees API (before: 16.0 degrees API or less; after: 20.0 degrees API or less) and Executive Order 12189 (1980-01-16) restated the order to read as follows, exempting heavy crude oil as defined by period: 16.0 degrees API or less for August 17 to December 20, 1979 and 20.0 degrees API or less from December 21, 1979. These are strike-and-insert amendments under owner ruling 2026-10-21; the clause continues, amended, and the rewrite changed the substance of the definition. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express deletion. Section 1-102 directed the Secretary of Energy to conduct a public inquiry on what other types of heavy crude oil should be exempt and to make a recommendation to the President. Executive Order 12186 of December 21, 1979 (44 FR 76477, Federal Register of December 27, 1979; held government printing) amends this order by deleting section 1-102; it states no effective date, so the end is dated on signing, 1979-12-21 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). Executive Order 12189 (1980-01-16) restated the order without restoring the inquiry, and Executive Order 12553 of 1986-02-25 later revoked the order by number; both are later events because the clause had already ended. No earlier end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12153, whose subject line describes decontrolling heavy oil. Section 1-103 lets the Secretary of Energy adopt regulations to implement the order under Executive Order 11790 as amended by Executive Order 12038. Executive Order 12186 renumbered it as section 1-102 (1979-12-21) and Executive Order 12189 restated it as section 1-104 (1980-01-16); these are amendments, later events, and the clause continues amended. No earlier express end was found.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12153 (44 FR 48949, Federal Register of August 21, 1979; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Decontrol of Heavy Oil and signed August 17, 1979. The dossier recorded the three numbered sections as one whole clause; they are separate commands with different fates (section 1-102 was deleted by a later order), so the inventory is corrected to sections 1-101, 1-102 and 1-103 using absolute spans of the held original. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12153, whose subject line describes decontrolling heavy oil. Section 1-102 ended earlier on 1979-12-21 by deletion; sections 1-101 and 1-103 end on 1986-02-25 and the whole-order end is the later date. Whether the authority of the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973 lapsed before 1986 is not established from held sources (the statute text is not held), and such a lapse would be an unnamed instrument and a disclosed candidate only. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12186, whose subject line describes changing the definition of heavy oil. The single instruction amends Executive Order 12153 by deleting section 1-102, renumbering section 1-103 as 1-102, and replacing the figure 16.0 degrees API with 20.0 degrees API in section 1-101. That is a strike-and-insert rewrite under owner ruling 2026-10-21: the clause continues, amended, and the substance of the definition changed. Whether the authority of the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973 lapsed before 1986 is not established from held sources (the statute text is not held), and such a lapse would be an unnamed instrument and a disclosed candidate only. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms. Section 1-105 provides that the Board terminates on December 31, 1981, unless sooner extended. The stated day is recorded inclusively, so the order is treated as running through the end of December 31, 1981 and the first end is dated 1981-12-31; on the exclusive reading (the order ends when that day begins) the end falls on 1981-12-30, disclosed for the reviewer (owner ruling 2026-10-21, until-dates). No extension is held: the packet’s number-citation lookup found no held text citing this order by number, and a name search of the held order texts for the Board found only its own printings, the American Presidency Project copy and the table of EO 12553. The rest of the clause establishes a 15-member National Advisory Community Investment Board under section 704 of the Economic Opportunity Act of 1964, assigns its functions as that section provides, directs the Community Services Administration Director to give administrative support, and assigns the Federal Advisory Committee Act functions of the President to that Director. All of it is time-limited by the same sunset. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 later revoked the order by number (the table lists 12254, whose subject line describes establishing the National Advisory Community Investment Board); it is a later event because the order had already ended. No earlier end was found.

By the authority vested in me as President of the United States o f A m erica by 
Section 704 of the Econom ic Opportunity A ct of 1964, as am ended (42 U.S.C. 
2981c), and in order to establish a N ational Advisory Community Investm ent 
Board, in accord with the Federal A dvisory Com m ittee A ct, as am ended (5 
U.S.C. App. I), it is hereby ordered as follow s:
1-101. There is established a N ational A dvisory Community Investm ent Board 
w hich shall be com posed of fifteen m em bers in accord w ith Section 704 of the 
Econom ic Opportunity A ct of 1964, as am ended (42 U.S.C. 2981c).
1-102. The Board shall perform the functions and carry out its activities as 
provided by Section 704 of the Econom ic Opportunity A ct o f 1964, as am ended 
(42 U.S.C. 2981c).
1-103. The D irector of the Community Services A dm inistration shall provide 
the Board w ith such adm inistrative services and support as m ay be n ecessary.
1-104. N otw ithstanding the provisions of any other E xecutive order, the 
functions of the President under the Federal A dvisory Com m ittee A ct (5 U .S.C. 
App. I), excep t that of reporting annually to the Congress, w hich are applica­
ble to the Board, shall be perform ed by the D irector of the Community 
Services A dm inistration in accord ance w ith guidelines and procedures estab ­
lished by the A dm inistrator of G eneral Services.
1-105. The Board shall term inate on D ecem ber 31, 1981, unless sooner ex ­
tended.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12257, whose subject line describes noncompetitive conversion of CETA participants to career or career-conditional civil service status. Sections 1-101 to 1-106 let Executive agencies, with the approval of the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, give excepted appointments up to grade GS-3 to persons who completed Comprehensive Employment and Training Act job training or a hosted work experience program within three months, allow noncompetitive conversion to career or career-conditional appointment after six months of satisfactory service, and direct the Director to issue guidelines and regulations. No earlier express end was found.

By the authority vested in me as President of the United States of A m erica by 
Sections 3301 and 3302 of Title 5 of the United States Code, and to provide 
opportunities for unemployed or disadvantaged persons to enter the Federal 
Civil Service, it is hereby ordered as fo llo w s:;
1-101. Su b ject to the Civil Service law s, rules, and regulations, Executive 
-agencies may, su bject to approval by the D irector of the O ffice of Personnel 
M anagem ent, give excepted appointm ents to qualified persons who have 
successfully com pleted jo b  training funded through the Com prehensive Em­
ployment and Training A ct, as am ended {29 U .S.C. 801 e t  s e q .) or a work 
experience program hosted by an Executive agency under this statute.
1-102. Such appointm ents may be to any position up to and including G S-3, or 
the equivalent thereof, for w hich the appointee is otherw ise qualified under 
the Civil Service law s, rules, and regulations.
1-103. No one shall be eligible for such an appointm ent if more than three 
m onths have expired since the successful com pletion of the job training or 
work experience program.
1-104. Excepted appointm ents under the authority of this Order are only 
authorized pursuant to an em ploym ent training program developed by an 
agency in accord ance w ith guidelines established by the O ffice of Personnel 
M anagem ent. T h ese guidelines w ill provide for due credit for training acquired 
during a hosted w ork experience program. Continued em ploym ent under such 
excepted appointm ents is su bject to the satisfactory  perform ance o f assigned 
duties and satisfactory participation in such em ploym ent training program.
1-105. An agency m ay noncom petitively convert an excepted appointm ent 
under this authority to career or career-conditional appointm ent, provided the 
appointee satisfactorily com pletes at least six m onths of continuous service, 
and otherw ise m eets the qualifications and other requirem ents established by 
the D irector of the O ffice of Personnel M anagem ent. Prior to an individual 
being converted to a career or career-conditional appointment, each agency 
shall conduct a careful and form al evaluation of the individual’s perform ance.
1-106. The D irector of the O ffice of Personnel M anagem ent shall issue em ploy­
ment training program guidelines w hich shall include procedures for periodi­
cally evaluating the perform ance of such appointees and for the prompt 
separation of those who do not satisfactorily perform assigned duties. The 
D irector shall also prescribe such regulations as m ay be n ecessary  to im ple­
ment this Order.

authorized pursuant to an em ploym ent training program developed by an

under this authority to career or career-conditional appointm ent, provided the 
appointee satisfactorily com pletes at least six m onths of continuous service, 
and otherw ise m eets the qualifications and other requirem ents established by 
the D irector of the O ffice of Personnel M anagem ent. Prior to an individual 
being converted to a career or career-conditional appointment, each agency 
shall conduct a careful and form al evaluation of the individual’s perform ance.

ment training program guidelines w hich shall include procedures for periodi­
cally evaluating the perform ance of such appointees and for the prompt 
separation of those who do not satisfactorily perform assigned duties. The

ment this Order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12263, whose subject line describes delegating strategic and critical materials transaction authority to the United States Trade Representative. The single paragraph delegates to the United States Trade Representative the functions vested in the President by section 5 of the Strategic and Critical Materials Transaction Authorization Act of 1979 in order to provide for the contribution of tin to the Tin Buffer Stock established under the Fifth International Tin Agreement. No earlier express end was found.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
Statutes of the United States o f A m erica, including the Strategic and C ritical 
M aterials T ransaction A uthorization A ct of 1979 (93 Stat. 1289; Public Law  9 6 - 
175) (hereinafter referred to as “the A ct”) and Section 301 o f Title 3 of the 
United States Code, and in order to provide for the contribution of tin to the 
Tin Buffer Stock established under the Fifth International Tin Agreem ent, the 
functions vested in the President by Section 5 of the A ct are hereby delegated 
to the United States Trade Representative.

It delegates the President’s functions under Public Law 96-599 to the United States Trade Representative. Inventory: two numbered sections, each recorded as one clause and confirmed against the full held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12297, whose subject line describes executing the International Coffee Agreement of 1976. The order has no sunset or deadline. The statute and the Agreement are not held; any expiry is an unnamed instrument and a disclosed candidate only (owner ruling 2026-10-21, unnamed instruments).  The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms. Section 1-105 provides that the exemptions granted by the order are for the one-year period beginning October 2, 1981, and ending October 1, 1982. The end date is recorded inclusively as 1982-10-01 (the order runs through the end of that day); on the exclusive reading the exemptions end when October 1, 1982 begins, disclosed for the reviewer (owner ruling 2026-10-21, until-dates). The order exempts each effluent source, emission source, noise-producing activity or facility and solid waste facility at Fort Allen in Puerto Rico from the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, the Clean Air Act, the Noise Control Act of 1972 and the Solid Waste Disposal Act (with listed exceptions) for the temporary housing of Haitian nationals; every exemption in sections 1-101 to 1-104 is limited by section 1-105. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 later revoked the order by number (the table lists 12327, whose subject line describes exempting Fort Allen from pollution control statutes); it is a later event because the order had already ended. No earlier end was found.

1-105. The exem ptions granted by this O rder shall be for the one-year period 
beginning O ctober 2,1981, and ending O ctober 1,1982.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12373 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The three numbered paragraphs (1-101 to 1-103) establish a three-member board effective immediately under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, direct it to report within 30 days from the date of its establishment, and restate the section 10 status-quo period from creation until 30 days after the report. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end; when it ran out depends on the unrecorded report date. No earlier express end was found.

Executive Order 12373 of July 21, 1982
Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute  
Between The United Transportation Union and Certain Rail­
roads Represented by the National Carriers' Conference Com­
m ittee of the National Railway Labor Conference
A dispute exists between the United Transportation Union and certain rail­
roads represented by the National Carriers’  Conference Committee of the  
National Railway Labor Conference designated on the list attached hereto and  
made a part hereof.
This dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
This dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, threatens  
substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a  
section of the country of essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 10 of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C.§160), it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
1-101. E stablish m en t o f Board. There is established, effective immediately, a  
board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this  
dispute. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested  
in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
1-102. R eport. The board' shall report its finding to the President with respect  
to the dispute within 30 days from the date of its establishment.
1-103. M aintaining Conditions.  As provided by Section 10 of the Railway  
Labor Act, as amended, from the date of the creation of the Emergency Board  
and for 30 days after the board has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be made by the carriers or by their  
employees, in the conditions out of which the dispute arose.

Executive Order 12373 of July 21, 1982
Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute  
Between The United Transportation Union and Certain Rail­
roads Represented by the National Carriers' Conference Com­
m ittee of the National Railway Labor Conference
A dispute exists between the United Transportation Union and certain rail­
roads represented by the National Carriers’  Conference Committee of the  
National Railway Labor Conference designated on the list attached hereto and  
made a part hereof.
This dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
This dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, threatens  
substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a  
section of the country of essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 10 of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C.§160), it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
1-101. E stablish m en t o f Board. There is established, effective immediately, a  
board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this  
dispute. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested  
in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
1-102. R eport. The board' shall report its finding to the President with respect  
to the dispute within 30 days from the date of its establishment.
1-103. M aintaining Conditions.  As provided by Section 10 of the Railway  
Labor Act, as amended, from the date of the creation of the Emergency Board  
and for 30 days after the board has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be made by the carriers or by their  
employees, in the conditions out of which the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12384 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The five numbered paragraphs (1-101 to 1-105) establish, effective October 1, 1982, a three-member board under section 510 of the Rail Passenger Service Act (45 U.S.C. 590), subject to the availability of funds, and direct a public hearing, an initial report within 30 days after creation, the submission of final offers if the dispute is not settled within ten days after the report, and a final report within 15 days after the final offers. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. No earlier express end was found.

Title 3— Executive Order 12384 of October 1, 1982
The President Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute  
Between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Au­
thority and the Delaware Transportation. Authority, and  
Certain Labor Organizations
A dispute exists between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Au­
thority (SEPTA) and the Delaware Transportation Authority (DTA), and  
certain labor organizations, designated on the list attached hereto and made a  
part hereof, representing those employees of the Consolidated Rail Corpora­
tion (Conrail) who are to be transferred to the SEPTA and DTA as part of the  
transfer of commuter fail service responsibility from Conrail to the SEPTA and  
DTA, pursuant to Section 1145 of the Northeast Rail Service Act of 1981.
The dispute concerns the terms and conditions of new collective bargaining  
agreements, which were required to be negotiated by September 1, 1982, by  
Section 510(a) of the Rail Passenger Service Act, as amended (“the Act”). As  
of this date, the parties have not entered into new collective bargaining  
agreements, and the SEPTA, the Northeast Commuter Services Corporation,  
and the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers have requested the President to  
establish an emergency board pursuant to Section 510(b) of the Act.
Section 510(c) of the Act provides for the President, upon request of a party, to  
appoint an emergency board to investigate such dispute and to make a report  
and recommendation for settlement.
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 510 of the Rail  
Passenger Service Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. § 590), it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
1-101. E sta b lish m en t o f  B oard. There is established, effective October 1,1982,  
a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this  
dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any commuter authority providing  
commuter rail service. The Board shall perform its functions subject to the  
availability of funds.
1-102. P u b lic H ea rin g. The board shall conduct a public hearing on the dispute  
at which each party shall appear and provide testimony.
1-103. In itia l R eport. The board shall report on the dispute within 30 days 
after the date of its creation.
1-104. F in a l O ffers. If the parties have not settled the dispute within ten days  
after the board’s report, the board shall require the parties to submit, within  
five days, their final offers for settlement of the dispute.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12385 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The five numbered paragraphs (1-101 to 1-105) establish, effective October 1, 1982, a three-member board under section 510 of the Rail Passenger Service Act (45 U.S.C. 590), subject to the availability of funds, and direct a public hearing, an initial report within 30 days after creation, the submission of final offers if the dispute is not settled within ten days after the report, and a final report within 15 days after the final offers. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. No earlier express end was found.

pursuant to Section 1145 o f the N ortheast R ail Service A ct of 1981.
The dispute concerns the terms and conditions of new collective bargaining  
agreements, which were required to be negotiated by September 1, 1982, by  
Section 510(a) of the Rail Passenger Service Act, as amended (“the Act”). As  
of this date, the parties have not entered into new collective bargaining  
agreements, and the N JTRO and the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers  
have requested the President to establish an emergency board pursuant to  
Section 510(b) of the Act.
Section 510(c) of the Act provides for the President, upon request of a party, to  
appoint an emergency board to investigate such dispute and to make a report  
and recommendation for settlement.
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 510 of the Rail  
Passenger Service Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. § 590), it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
1-101. E sta b lish m en t o f  B oard. There is established, effective October 1, 1982,  
a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this  
dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any 
organization of railroad employees or any commuter authority, providing  
commuter rail service. The Board shall perform its functions subject to the  
availability of funds.
1-102. P u b lic H ea rin g. The board shall conduct a public hearing on the dispute 
at w hich each party shall appear and provide testim ony.
1-103. In itia l R eport. The board shall report on the dispute within 30 days  
after the date of its creation.
1-104. F in a l O ffers. If the parties have not settled the dispute within ten days  
after the board’s report, the board shall require the parties to submit, within  
five days, their final offers for settlement of the dispute.

Executive Order 12385 of October 1, 1982

Between New Jersey Transit Rail Operations, Inc. and Certain  
Labor Organizations
A  dispute exists betw een New Jersey T ransit R ail O perations, Inc. (NJTRO), 
and certain lab or organizations, designated on the list attached hereto and 
m ade a part hereof, representing those em ployees of the C onsolidated Rail 
Corporation (Conrail) who are to be transferred to the NJTRO as part of the 
transfer of com m uter r a il,  service responsibility from Conrail to the NJTRO, 
pursuant to Section 1145 o f the N ortheast R ail Service A ct of 1981.

agreements, which were required to be negotiated by September 1, 1982, by  
Section 510(a) of the Rail Passenger Service Act, as amended (“the Act”). As  
of this date, the parties have not entered into new collective bargaining  
agreements, and the N JTRO and the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers  
have requested the President to establish an emergency board pursuant to  
Section 510(b) of the Act.

appoint an emergency board to investigate such dispute and to make a report  
and recommendation for settlement.

Passenger Service Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. § 590), it is hereby ordered as
