a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this  
dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any 
organization of railroad employees or any commuter authority, providing  
commuter rail service. The Board shall perform its functions subject to the  
availability of funds.
1-102. P u b lic H ea rin g. The board shall conduct a public hearing on the dispute 
at w hich each party shall appear and provide testim ony.
1-103. In itia l R eport. The board shall report on the dispute within 30 days  
after the date of its creation.

after the board’s report, the board shall require the parties to submit, within  
five days, their final offers for settlement of the dispute.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12386 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The five numbered paragraphs (1-101 to 1-105) establish, effective October 1, 1982, a three-member board under section 510 of the Rail Passenger Service Act (45 U.S.C. 590), subject to the availability of funds, and direct a public hearing, an initial report within 30 days after creation, the submission of final offers if the dispute is not settled within ten days after the report, and a final report within 15 days after the final offers. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. No earlier express end was found.

Executive Order 12386 of October 1, 1982
Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute  
Between the New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority  
and the Connecticut Department of Transportation, and Certain  
Labor Organizations
A dispute exists between the New York Metropolitan Transportation Authori­
ty (MTA) and the Connecticut Department of Transportation (CDOT), and  
certain labor organizations, designated on the list attached hereto and made a  
part hereof, representing those employees of the Consolidated Rail Corpora­
tion (Conrail) who are to be transferred to the MTA and CDOT as part of the  
transfer of commuter rail service responsibility from Conrail to the MTA and  
CDOT, pursuant to Section 1145 of the Northeast Rail Service Act of 1981.
The dispute concerns the terms and conditions of new collective bargaining  
agreements, which were required to be negotiated by September 1, 1982, b jy  
Section 510(a) of the Rail Passenger Service Act, as amended (“the Act”). As  
of this date, the parties have not entered into new collective bargaining  
agreements, and the MTA and the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers have  
requested the President to establish an emergency board pursuant to Section  
510(b) of the Act.
Section 510(c) of the Act provides for the President, upon request of a party, to  
appoint an emergency board to investigate such dispute and to make a report  
and recommendation for settlement.
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 510 of the Rail  
Passenger Service Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. § 590), it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
1-101. Establishm ent o f Board. There is established, effective October 1,1982,  
a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this  
dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any commuter authority providing  
commuter rail service. The Board shall perform its functions subject to the  
availability of funds.
1-102. Public H earing. The board shall conduct a public hearing on the dispute  
at which each party shall appear and provide testimony.
1-103. Initial Report.  The board shall report on the dispute within 30 days  
after the date of its creation.
1-104. Final O ffers. If the parties have not settled the dispute within ten days  
after the board’s report, the board shall require, the parties to submit, within  
five days, their final offers for settlement of the dispute.

1-105. F in a l re p o rt. W ithin 15 days after the subm ission of final offers, the 
board shall submit a report to the President setting forth its selection of the 
most reasonable offer.

Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12390, whose subject line describes delegating a reporting function to the Secretary of State concerning U.S. credit to Poland. Section 1 delegates to the Secretary of State the functions vested in the President by section 306 of the Supplemental Appropriations Act of 1982 (Public Law 97-257). No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12390, whose subject line describes delegating a reporting function to the Secretary of State concerning U.S. credit to Poland. Section 2 directs the Secretary of State, before making the determination and written reports referred to in that section 306, to confer with the Secretary of the Treasury and, as appropriate, the Secretary of Agriculture and other interested agency heads. No earlier express end was found.

Title 3—
The President
Executive Order 12390 of October 25, 1982
Delegation to the Secretary of State
By the authority vested in me as President of the United States of America by  
Section 301 of Title 3 of the United States Code, in order to assign certain  
functions to the Secretary of State, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. The functions vested in the President by Section 306 of the  
Supplemental Appropriations Act of 1982 (Public Law 97-257) are delegated to  
the Secretary of State.
Sec. 2. Before making the determination and providing the written reports  
referred to in that Section 306, the Secretary of State shall confer with the  
Secretary of the Treasury and, as appropriate, with the Secretary of Agricul­
ture and the heads of other interested Executive agencies.
Sec. 3. Similar functions vested in the President by Section 205 of Public Law  
97-216 were delegated to the Secretary of State. The performance by the  
Secretary of State of those functions is confirmed and ratified.
THE WHITE HOUSE,  
O ctober 25, 1982.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by performance on issuance. Section 3 states that similar functions vested in the President by section 205 of Public Law 97-216 were delegated to the Secretary of State and that the Secretary’s performance of those functions is confirmed and ratified. The ratification was complete when the order was signed on 1982-10-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer), and it contains no continuing command; the ratified acts are a surviving consequence recorded under savings, and a later revocation does not show a first cessation of a command already performed. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 later revoked the order by number; it is a later event because this clause had already ended. No earlier end was found.

Title 3—
The President
Executive Order 12390 of October 25, 1982
Delegation to the Secretary of State
By the authority vested in me as President of the United States of America by  
Section 301 of Title 3 of the United States Code, in order to assign certain  
functions to the Secretary of State, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. The functions vested in the President by Section 306 of the  
Supplemental Appropriations Act of 1982 (Public Law 97-257) are delegated to  
the Secretary of State.
Sec. 2. Before making the determination and providing the written reports  
referred to in that Section 306, the Secretary of State shall confer with the  
Secretary of the Treasury and, as appropriate, with the Secretary of Agricul­
ture and the heads of other interested Executive agencies.
Sec. 3. Similar functions vested in the President by Section 205 of Public Law  
97-216 were delegated to the Secretary of State. The performance by the  
Secretary of State of those functions is confirmed and ratified.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12390 (47 FR 47799, Federal Register of October 28, 1982; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Delegation to the Secretary of State and signed October 25, 1982. It delegates the President’s functions under section 306 of Public Law 97-257 to the Secretary of State and ratifies the Secretary’s earlier performance of similar functions under Public Law 97-216. Inventory: three numbered sections, each recorded as one clause and confirmed against the full held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12390, whose subject line describes delegating a reporting function to the Secretary of State concerning U.S. credit to Poland. Sections 1 and 2 end on that date; section 3 is a ratification exhausted on issuance, so the whole-order end is the later date. Whether the statutory authority lapsed earlier is not established (the statutes are not held) and would be an unnamed instrument and a disclosed candidate only.  The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12392, whose subject line describes delegating authority to the Secretary of the Treasury to make payments to certain international financial institutions. The single paragraph delegates to the Secretary of the Treasury the functions vested in the President by section 129 of Public Law 97-276 (October 2, 1982), which concern making payments to certain international financial institutions. No earlier express end was found.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of  
the United States of America, including Section 301 of Title 3 of the United  
States Code, and in order to assign to the Secretary of the Treasury the  
authority to make payments to certain international financial institutions, it is  
hereby ordered that the functions vested in the President by Section 129 of  
Public Law 97-276 (October 2, 1982) are delegated to the Secretary of the  
Treasury.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12405 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The four numbered paragraphs (1-101 to 1-104) establish a three-member board effective immediately under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, direct a report within 30 days of its creation, restate the section 10 status-quo period until 30 days after the report, and provide that the board terminates upon submission of the report. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end; when it ran out depends on the unrecorded report date. This clause provides that the board terminates on or after the submission of its report. The report date is not held in this packet’s citable evidence, and the clause is read as a report-relative sunset that is functionally spent on the report date and not as the end, by analogy to owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C), which that ruling applies to report-relative sunsets of other boards; this analogy is a reading disclosed for the reviewer. No earlier express end was found.

Executive Order 12405 of February 14, 1983
Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute 
Between the Consolidated Rail Corporation and the Brother­
hood of Locomotive Engineers
À dispute exists between the Consolidated Rail Corporation and the Brother­
hood of Locomotive Engineers.
The dispute has not heretofore been adjusted Under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (“the Act”).
This dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, threatens  
substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a 
section of the country of essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 10 of the Act, as 
amended (45 U.S.C. § 160), it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-101. Establishment o f Board. There is established, effective immediately,  
a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this 
dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
1-102. Report  The board shall report its findings to the President with respect 
to the dispute within 30 days of its creation.
1— 103. Maintaining Conditions. As provided by Section T O  of the Act, as  
amended, from the date of the creation of the Emergency Board, and for 30  
days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by 
agreement of the parties, shall be made by the carrier or by the employees, in 
the conditions out of which the dispute arose.
1-104. Expiration. The Emergency Board shall terminate upon submission of  
the report provided for in paragraph 1-102 of this Order.

days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12414 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 1 establishes, effective immediately, a three-member board under section 9A of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 159a). The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12414 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 2 requires the parties to submit final offers within 30 days after creation of the board and the board to report its selection of the most reasonable offer within 30 days after the final offers. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12414 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 3 restates the section 9A(h) status-quo period, from the request to establish a board until 60 days after the board’s report. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end; when it ran out depends on the unrecorded report date. No earlier express end was found.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Sec. 3. M aintaining C onditions. As provided by Section 9A(h) of the Act, as 
amended, from the time a request to establish a board is made until 60 days 
after the board makes its report, no change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the parties in the conditions out of which the dispute arose.

Executive Order 12414 of April 4, 1983
Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute  
Between The Long- Island Rail Road and Certain Labor Orga­
nizations
A dispute exists between The Long Island Rail Road and certain labor 
organizations, designated on the list attached hereto and made a part hereof, 
representing employees of The Long Island Rail Road.
The dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the 
Railway Labor Act, as amended ("the Act”).
The New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the parent body of The 
Long Island Rail Road, has requested that the President establish an emergen­
cy board pursuant to Section 9A of the Act.
Section 9A(e) of the Act provides that the President, upon request of a party, 
shall appoint an emergency board to investigate and report on the dispute.
NOW, THEREFORE, by tha. authority vested in me by Section 9A of the Act, 
as amended (45 U.S.C. § 159a), it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. E stablish m en t o f  B oard. There is established, effective immediately, 
a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this 
dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any 
organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
Sec. 2. R eport. Within 30 days after creation of the board the parties to the 
dispute shall submit to the board final offers for settlement of the dispute. 
Within 30 days after the submission of final offers the board shall submit a 
report to the President setting forth its selection of the most reasonable offer.
Sec. 3. M aintaining C onditions. As provided by Section 9A(h) of the Act, as 
amended, from the time a request to establish a board is made until 60 days 
after the board makes its report, no change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the parties in the conditions out of which the dispute arose.
Sec. 4. E xpiration . The Emergency Board shall terminate upon submission of 
the report provided for in Sec. 2 of this Order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12440, whose subject line describes increasing the membership of the President’s Commission on Industrial Competitiveness. The single sentence amends the second sentence of section 1(a) of Executive Order 12428 of June 28, 1983 so that the President’s Commission on Industrial Competitiveness is composed of no more than thirty members appointed or designated by the President. Executive Order 12457 of January 3, 1984 amended the same sentence again (before: no more than thirty members; after: no more than thirty-five members); under owner ruling 2026-10-21 that is a strike-and-insert amendment, the clause continues, amended, and the membership ceiling changed. Executive Order 12534 of September 30, 1985 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) revokes the parent order 12428 but does not name this order; under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments) it is a disclosed candidate earlier end for the reviewer and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12442, whose subject line describes continuing the President’s Commission on Indian Reservation Economies. Section 1 amends section 2(d) of Executive Order 12401 so that the Commission submits its final report to the President and the Secretary of the Interior by November 30, 1984. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the Commission reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. Executive Order 12534 of September 30, 1985 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) revokes the parent order 12401 but does not name this order; under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments) it is a disclosed candidate earlier end for the reviewer and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12442, whose subject line describes continuing the President’s Commission on Indian Reservation Economies. Section 2 amends section 4(b) of Executive Order 12401 so that the Commission, unless sooner extended, terminates 30 days after it transmits its final report to the President. This is a report-relative sunset: its date depends on the date the final report was transmitted, which is not held in this packet’s citable evidence, and it is treated as functionally spent on that date and not as the end, by analogy to owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C), which that ruling applies to report-relative sunsets; this analogy is a reading disclosed for the reviewer. Executive Order 12534 of September 30, 1985 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) revokes the parent order 12401 but does not name this order; under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments) it is a disclosed candidate earlier end for the reviewer and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. No earlier express end was found.

Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12449, whose subject line describes continuing the National Bipartisan Commission on Central America. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12449, whose subject line describes continuing the National Bipartisan Commission on Central America. The amended text provides that the Commission shall report to the President by February 1, 1984. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the Commission reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. Executive Order 12534 of September 30, 1985 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) revokes the parent order 12433 but does not name this order; under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments) it is a disclosed candidate earlier end for the reviewer and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12457, whose subject line describes continuing the President’s Commission on Industrial Competitiveness and increasing its membership. The lead-in amends Executive Order 12428 of June 28, 1983, as amended, to increase the membership and extend the life of the President’s Commission on Industrial Competitiveness. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12457, whose subject line describes continuing the President’s Commission on Industrial Competitiveness and increasing its membership. Paragraph (a) rewrites the second sentence of section 1(a) of Executive Order 12428 so that the Commission is composed of no more than thirty-five members appointed or designated by the President. Whether the end of the Commission’s life extinguished this membership ceiling is not shown by a held source, so the first held end of this clause is the revocation. Executive Order 12534 of September 30, 1985 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) revokes the parent order 12428 but does not name this order; under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments) it is a disclosed candidate earlier end for the reviewer and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. No earlier express end was found.

Paragraph (b) rewrites section 4(b) of Executive Order 12428 to provide that the Commission terminates on December 31, 1984, unless sooner extended. The stated day is recorded inclusively, so the first end is dated 1984-12-31; on the exclusive reading the end falls on 1984-12-30, disclosed for the reviewer (owner ruling 2026-10-21, until-dates). No extension is held: a number search of the held Federal Register order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts) for the parent order 12428 found citations only in Executive Orders 12440, 12457 and 12534. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 later revoked this order by number (the table lists 12457, whose subject line describes continuing the President’s Commission on Industrial Competitiveness and increasing its membership); it is a later event because the clause had already ended. Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12457 (49 FR 865, Federal Register of January 6, 1984; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed President’s Commission on Industrial Competitiveness and signed January 3, 1984. It increases the membership and extends the life of the President’s Commission on Industrial Competitiveness. Inventory: the lead-in and paragraphs (a) and (b), each recorded as one clause and confirmed against the full held text. Ending: Paragraph (b) ended on its own sunset (1984-12-31, inclusive); the lead-in and paragraph (a) end on EO 12553 (1986-02-25), so the whole-order end is the later date. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12457, whose subject line describes continuing the President’s Commission on Industrial Competitiveness and increasing its membership.  The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12476, whose subject line describes relating to the Presidential Commission on the Conduct of United States-Japan Relations. The lead-in amends Executive Order 12421 of May 12, 1983, which created the Presidential Commission on the Conduct of United States-Japan Relations. Executive Order 12534 of September 30, 1985 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) revokes the parent order 12421 but does not name this order; under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments) it is a disclosed candidate earlier end for the reviewer and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12476, whose subject line describes relating to the Presidential Commission on the Conduct of United States-Japan Relations. Section 1 replaces the phrase Advisory Group on United States-Japan Relations with United States-Japan Advisory Commission in sections 1(b), 2(b) and 2(d) and replaces the words This group with This bi-national group in section 2(b). No earlier express end was found.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Section 1. Sections 1(b), 2(b) and 2(d) are amended by deleting, the phrase  
“Advisory Group on United States-Japan Relations” in each Section and  
inserting instead the phrase “United States-Japan Advisory Commission.”  
Section 2(b) is further amended by deleting the phrase “This group” and  
inserting instead the phrase “This bi-national group.”

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12476, whose subject line describes relating to the Presidential Commission on the Conduct of United States-Japan Relations. Section 2 rewrites section 2(c) so that the Commission, in connection with its participation in the United States-Japan Advisory Commission, may conduct studies, hearings and meetings, assemble and disseminate information, and issue reports and other publications. Whether the end of the Commission’s life extinguished this power is not shown by a held source, so the first held end of this clause is the revocation. No earlier express end was found.

participation in the United States-Japan Advisory Commission, the Commis­
sion may conduct studies, hearings, and meetings as it deems necessary;  
assemble and disseminate information; and issue reports and other publica­
tions.”

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms. Section 3 rewrites section 4(b) of Executive Order 12421 to provide that, in accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act, the Commission terminates on October 31, 1984, unless sooner extended. The stated day is recorded inclusively, so the first end is dated 1984-10-31; on the exclusive reading the end falls on 1984-10-30, disclosed for the reviewer (owner ruling 2026-10-21, until-dates). No extension is held: a number search of the held Federal Register order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts) for the parent order 12421 found citations only in Executive Orders 12476 and 12534. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 later revoked this order by number (the table lists 12476, whose subject line describes relating to the Presidential Commission on the Conduct of United States-Japan Relations); it is a later event because the clause had already ended. No earlier end was found.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12476 (49 FR 20473, Federal Register of May 15, 1984; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Presidential Commission on the Conduct of United States-Japan Relations and signed May 11, 1984. It renames the advisory group the Commission works with, rewrites the Commission’s powers and sets its termination date. Inventory: the lead-in and sections 1 to 3, each recorded as one clause and confirmed against the full held text. Ending: Section 3 ended on its own sunset (1984-10-31, inclusive); the lead-in and sections 1 and 2 end on EO 12553 (1986-02-25), so the whole-order end is the later date. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12476, whose subject line describes relating to the Presidential Commission on the Conduct of United States-Japan Relations. Executive Order 12534 of September 30, 1985 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) revokes the parent order 12421 but does not name this order; under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments) it is a disclosed candidate earlier end for the reviewer and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event.  The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).
